response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position), s AS (SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, attendance_count * 1.0 / SUM(attendance_count) OVER () AS share FROM c), r AS (SELECT s.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rnk FROM s) SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, share FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC, member_id

assumptions.assumption: Share is the group's count divided by the sum of counts across all member/position groups, expressed as a fraction (0-1) rather than a percentage.
Ties at the 10th place are included by using RANK() over share, so rows with the same share as the 10th row are kept.
Attendance records with no matching member are dropped by the inner join; members with no attendance do not appear.
